proofUses.reason: Finite-product pivotality is taken with its bond deleted. Finite polynomial maxima are locally Lipschitz, with explicit one-sided derivatives. Reciprocal bounds pass pointwise through finite-volume exhaustion.

The proved intensity derivative inequality is converted to bond probability, retaining its factor 1/(1-p), and integrated. Neighbouring open triangles must be uniformly smaller than one; bare diagonal finiteness is not substituted.

The finite triangle contains a bubble; uniqueness and Harris bound each connection below by theta squared. The three exponent inequalities follow independently from established susceptibility, density and field lower bounds.

The corrected quadratic boundary inequality, right-open finite susceptibility and reciprocal integration give the finite-triangle endpoint estimate. Existing entropy and tail-field arguments supply the critical laws without smallness.
Normalized lattice weights identify the susceptibility endpoint with the probability critical point. The exact probability-to-intensity conversion and sharpness give all classical mean-field orders.
